title: So be patient, the promise of Allah is true
summary: Doctrinal editorial arguing that patience (sabr) and certainty (yaqin) are the twin qualities that sustain the fighter and underwrite divine victory. It opens by noting that the Quranic command to patience recurs throughout the text and is repeatedly paired with a promise of victory, citing the close of Surat al-Rum and two verses of Surat Ghafir. It frames certainty as the conviction that drives a fighter to plunge into enemy ranks, and builds its case on classical exegetes (al-Tabari, Ibn al-Qayyim, al-Baghawi, al-Qurtubi, Ibn Kathir) and a contemporary IS shaykh, Abu Hudhayfa al-Ansari. The argument is inward-facing and concerned with morale: resolve eroded by repeated setbacks is to be mended through certainty and acceptance. It warns against defeatists weak in conviction who associate with doubters, and applies the prophetic image of recitation that does not pass the throat to present-day Muslims it judges insincere. It closes on governance, citing Quran 5:50 to argue that the people of certainty reject man-made law in favour of divine rule (hakimiyya).
keyClaims: Patience and certainty are the qualities that sustain the fighter and secure divine victory.
Allah's promise of victory is true and repeatedly paired in scripture with the command to patience.
Setbacks are tests to be endured through certainty, repentance and seeking forgiveness rather than abandoned.
Defeatists weak in conviction who mix with doubters expose themselves to ruin.
The people of certainty reject man-made law in favour of divine governance (hakimiyya).
significanceAssessment: The editorial is a steadfastness piece, not an operational or triumphalist one. Its sustained focus on enduring reversals and its explicit warning about defeatism within the ranks are consistent with IS messaging during periods of attrition, reframing setbacks as divinely ordained tests with victory deferred but certain. The citation of a contemporary shaykh alongside the theological scaffolding presents perseverance as doctrinally mandated rather than a matter of morale alone.
notes: Page 3 editorial clearly legible and analysed in full. Editorial is thematic and doctrinal, so no geographic or group references appear within it.
